headline: High risk of cascading errors and capability conflict; medium prompt-injection and data-leakage exposure from shared file-based workflows.

A_prompt_injection.rationale: mem0 is a knowledge-management agent with no network egress, but production-agentic-rag-course reads and writes files, runs subprocesses, and uses stdin/stdout in a local development environment. If mem0 outputs are copied into B’s file-based or prompt-based workflows, B may treat attacker-controlled memory text as instructions. The interaction is inferred, not directly documented, so uncertainty pushes to medium.
conditions: IF mem0 outputs are copied into files that B later ingests as prompts or instructions
IF B parses file or stdin/stdout content as trusted agent instructions
mitigations: Add a strict delimiter and schema for mem0 outputs before B consumes them
Review B prompts for any instruction-following over file content
Keep mem0 outputs in a separate directory from B inputs
Disable automatic ingestion of generated memory text into B
requires-engineering: add provenance tags and content filtering between agents

B_data_leakage.rationale: mem0 is a memory system and B explicitly handles configuration secrets plus academic papers and paper metadata. B has read/write filesystem access and allowlisted network egress, so if the pair shares a workspace, sensitive files can flow from B into mem0 or vice versa. The shared-workspace pathway is not explicitly stated, so this is inferred and kept at medium rather than high.
conditions: IF both agents operate in the same local workspace
IF B stores secrets or paper data in files that mem0 can read or summarize
mitigations: Store secrets in a separate vault outside the shared workspace
Restrict B to a dedicated input/output directory
Audit which files mem0 can access before running
Rotate any exposed API keys after shared-workspace runs
requires-engineering: enforce filesystem sandboxing between agents

C_capability_conflict.rationale: mem0 itself shows no write or network capabilities, while B can execute shell commands, install packages, spawn subprocesses, and write the filesystem. If both are pointed at the same directory, B can overwrite or race with mem0-managed artifacts even without git modification. Because shared mutable state is not stated, the conflict is plausible but not proven, so medium is appropriate.
conditions: IF both agents write to the same directory or cache
IF B runs multiple instances against shared mutable state
mitigations: Assign each agent its own working directory
Serialize writes with a simple lock file
Avoid concurrent runs during evaluation
Check for file ownership before B writes
requires-engineering: add orchestrator-level locking

D_cascading_error.rationale: mem0 is a memory/knowledge layer, so its outputs are likely to be treated as authoritative context by B’s agentic RAG workflow. B exposes /api/v1/ask and /api/v1/agentic-ask plus shell and filesystem actions, so a bad memory entry can cascade into incorrect content or actions. Because B has downstream action-taking authority and the pairwise handoff is a natural default pattern, the blast radius is high.
conditions: IF B uses mem0 output as retrieval context or system prompt material
IF B’s agentic-ask path acts on retrieved facts without verification
mitigations: Require human review before B acts on mem0-derived facts
Add a verification step against source documents
Mark mem0 output as untrusted context in B prompts
Log provenance for every mem0-derived claim
requires-engineering: implement citation-backed gating before actions

E_compliance.rationale: mem0 is a general knowledge-management system, while B explicitly handles configuration secrets and can run in a local development environment with allowlisted egress. If the pair shares files, retention or residency rules for secrets and research data can diverge, creating a compliance mismatch. No single residency violation is proven, so medium fits the documented policy mismatch risk.
conditions: IF secrets or regulated research data are stored in the shared workspace
IF mem0 retains data longer than the operator’s policy for B’s secrets or papers
mitigations: Separate regulated data from general memory storage
Document retention rules for both agents
Delete shared artifacts after each run
Review whether any secrets are written into mem0
requires-engineering: align retention and residency controls across both systems
